title: Optimizing Reactivity
description: Use shallowRef, shallowReactive, and avoid unnecessary reactivity.

slides.title: When Too Much Reactivity Hurts
slides.content:
# Avoid Deep Reactivity When Not Needed

Deep reactive objects (`reactive`) track changes at all nested levels. For large objects where only the top‑level changes matter, this overhead is unnecessary.

**Shallow variants**:
- `shallowRef` – only `.value` assignment is reactive; nested properties are not.
- `shallowReactive` – only first‑level properties are reactive.

Use them for large static data or when you only replace the whole object, not mutate it deeply.

slides.title: MarkRaw and readonly
slides.content:
# Other Tools

- `markRaw` – marks an object so that it will never be converted to a proxy. Useful for large third‑party objects or data that should remain static.
- `readonly` – creates a reactive object that is read‑only, preventing mutations. This can help avoid unintended changes and reduce reactivity overhead.

```javascript
import { markRaw } from 'vue'

const externalData = markRaw(heavyObject)
// now externalData is not reactive
```

quizData.question: What is the purpose of `shallowReactive`?

options.text: It makes an object deeply reactive
It makes only the first‑level properties reactive
It prevents the object from being reactive at all

quizData.explanation: `shallowReactive` creates a proxy that only tracks property access at the root level; nested properties are not reactive.
